question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

To meet one's eyes

options.text: To look at someone directly while they are looking at you

solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'** i.e. *"To look at someone directly while they are looking at you".*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"to meet one's eyes"** means *to make direct eye contact with someone*.(किसी से सीधे आँख मिलाना)
 
• When you "meet someone's eyes," you are looking directly into their eyes while they are looking back into yours.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is:* '**To look at someone directly while they are looking at you'*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's explain all the given options:
 
 
• **"To confess something"** - This is not the correct interpretation of the phrase. It refers to admitting or acknowledging a wrongdoing or a truth. (कुछ का इतराफ करना)
 
• **"To make haste"** - This means to hurry or to rush. It is not the correct interpretation of the phrase.(जल्दबाजी करना)
 
• **"To meet someone regularly"** - This refers to seeing or interacting with someone frequently, which is not the correct interpretation of the phrase.(नियमित रूप से किसी से मिलना)
